# Guide – ArtFlawless Studio workflow for Z-Image Turbo

Workflow & Studio created by Lalikavics. Every model, LoRA and custom node used here belongs to its own author.

## Layout – three blocks (left to right)
- **A · IMAGE INPUTS**: everything that needs a loaded image. Two columns: ① *image → prompt* (1a, 1d) and ② *image → image* (1e start image, 1b layout, 1c style). Each group has **its own ON/OFF switch right above it**: load the image and switch the group on in the same place.
- **B · WHAT & HOW**: the **Control panel** (group 0: THEME, ASPECT RATIO, DEFAULT LOOK, YOUR PROMPT, negative prompt, seed, base LoRA, additional LoRAs, models, and the Preset table at the bottom) and next to it **1. Base image** (sampler, preview, Final prompt).
- **C · POST-PROCESSING**: six ON/OFF switches at the top left (2, 3, 3b, 3c, 4, 5), followed by the steps in order.

## Quick start
1. **THEME**: pick what you are generating. The theme sets the opening and closing tags of the prompt, the image size, the shift, the base LoRA strength, and the denoise of the refine and final upscale steps.
2. **ASPECT RATIO**: `Theme default` = the theme's own size; every other option overrides it.
3. **YOUR PROMPT**: describe only what you want to see, in English. The theme adds the trigger and exclusion tags, so do not type them again.
4. **Run**. After the run the **Applied settings** box shows the values that were actually used and the steps recommended for the theme, and the **Final prompt** box (group 1) shows the full text sent to the model.

- **DEFAULT LOOK (Portrait, People)**: Z-Image Turbo tends to draw East Asian faces by default, and words like `caucasian` or `european girl` are not enough to change that. When the **DEFAULT LOOK** switch is ON, the two people themes write a European look into the prompt. It is OFF by default. If your prompt names another origin (for example `Japanese woman`, `African man`), the default look is left out automatically. The sentences and the exception words are the `look_pre`, `look_post` and `skip_words` lines of the Preset table. **Do not write `not asian`**: the negation has no effect while the word `asian` does (the panel removes it for you).
- **None (own prompt only)** theme: adds nothing to the prompt; shift 3, no base LoRA (0). If you want the base LoRA with this theme, switch **Manual strength** ON and set the value.
- **You still switch the steps (2, 3, 3b, 3c, 4, 5) yourself** with the switches at the top left of block C; the theme only prints a recommendation.
- **Switches**: click anywhere on the row to toggle. If the rows are drawn wider than the box, close the right-hand panel, switch to another workflow tab and back.
- **Values you no longer set by hand**: image size, shift, refine denoise and final upscale denoise are driven by the theme. To change them, edit the theme's row in the **Preset table** node.
- **Your own theme**: copy a row of the table under a new name, and type exactly the same name into the next empty `option` field of the THEME node.
- **When 1a or 1d is on, YOUR PROMPT is not used**: the image description or the embedded prompt is sent instead. The first line of Applied settings (`Prompt source`) shows which one is active.
- The theme tags are also added to the 1a description and the 1d embedded prompt; pick the `None` theme if you do not want that.
- The theme values are starting points: each was checked with a test image, but they are not fine-tuned.

## Z-Image Turbo notes
- **Three files are needed**: the model (checkpoint), the text encoder (Qwen3 4B, in `models\text_encoders`) and the VAE (Flux AE, in `models\vae`). The three loader nodes at the bottom of the right column of the Control panel load them.
- **Prompt**: Z-Image expects natural, sentence-style descriptions in English, not tags. That is why the 1a image description works especially well with it.
- **The negative prompt has almost no effect**, because the model runs at CFG 1. The box is still there, but do not rely on it.
- **Settings**: base image 9 steps, CFG 1, sampler res_multistep, scheduler simple. Do not change these much: higher CFG ruins the image. Refine, the detailers and the final upscale use the **euler** sampler, because res_multistep produced grainy skin there.
- **LoRA** (Control panel, right column): the **base LoRA** is `Hands + Feet + skin perfection style zib v1`. **BASE LoRA – ON/OFF**: when OFF it is never used. When ON the theme sets its strength (0.3–1.0; 0 for the `None` theme, so it is not used). **Manual strength – ON/OFF** and **Manual strength value**: when ON, the typed value is used instead of the theme's, so you can use the LoRA with the `None` theme too. Applied settings shows which one is active. Right below is the **Additional LoRAs** node: add as many as you like (➕ Add Lora), each with its own switch and strength; do not add the base LoRA there as well, or it acts twice. Only LoRAs made for Z-Image work; SDXL and Pony LoRAs do not.
- **Layout image and style image** (groups **1b** and **1c**): SDXL ControlNets and IPAdapter do not work with Z-Image, so the layout is transferred by Z-Image's own **Fun ControlNet Union 2.1 (lite)** model (`models\model_patches`), and the style by a style sentence extracted from an image description plus a color transfer.

## Step by step
1. Pick a theme, type the prompt into **YOUR PROMPT**, then **Run**. Only the base image is made.
2. Run again until you like the composition. The seed is random by default (-1), so every run gives a different image.
3. When the base image is good: press **♻️ Use Last Queued Seed** on the **Seed** node. This locks the image.
4. Switch on the next step in block C (2 → 3 → 4 → 5; the image inputs of block A – 1a, 1b, 1c, 1d, 1e – affect the base image, so set those at the beginning), then **Run**. With a fixed seed the finished steps are not run again, only the new one.
5. If a step makes the image worse: switch it off or lower its **denoise**.
6. For a new image: **🎲 Randomize Each Time**.

## Which step when
- **1a. Describe image → prompt** – if you do not want to write a prompt: load an image, Florence-2 describes it, and the description is used as the positive prompt instead of your text. The negative prompt stays the typed one.
- **1d. Read embedded prompt** – if the image was made with ComfyUI, A1111 or Forge, this reads the original positive AND negative prompt saved in the file and uses them instead of the typed ones.
- **1b. Layout reference** – to take over the composition of an existing image: where the big shapes are, what is in front and behind. Content, colors and style come from the prompt.
- **1c. Style reference** – to take over the color palette and mood of an image. The main prompt is always stronger. Works together with 1b or alone.
- **1e. Start image (img2img)** – to start from an existing image instead of an empty canvas: its shapes and colors stay and the prompt only rewrites them. 1b takes only the layout and 1c only the palette and mood; this one carries the image itself.
- **2. Refine** – almost always: more detail, sharper texture.
- **3. Face / 3b. Hand** – people only. Leave them off for landscapes, buildings, objects and abstract images.
- **3c. Foot** – people only, with its own foot detector. If no foot is found the image passes through unchanged. **Detected area preview** shows what was repainted. If only one foot is repainted or the selection is too tight, adjust the **Foot detailer** node: a lower `bbox_threshold` (default 0.25) finds more feet, `bbox_dilation` (default 40) enlarges the repainted area, and `bbox_crop_factor` (default 3) adds more surrounding context. A foot LoRA can be loaded in the **Foot LoRA** node (➕ Add Lora): it affects the foot detailer only.
- **4. Final upscale** – at the very end. This is the slowest step (several minutes).
- **5. Save** – when the image is finished. You can also save from a preview with a right click.
- The **Image Comparer** always shows the base image next to the result of the last active step.

## 1a. Describe image: notes
- The text is shown in the **Extracted description** box. To edit it: copy it into YOUR PROMPT, change it, and switch 1a off.
- **task**: `more_detailed_caption` = long description, `detailed_caption` = medium, `caption` = one sentence.
- The first run downloads the Florence-2 model (about 1.5 GB).

## 1d. Embedded prompt: notes
- The image is picked from the **input** folder (**source_folder** can be switched to output).
- It only works with images that contain a prompt. If there is none, the prompt will be empty: use 1a instead.
- When 1a and 1d are both on, 1d (the embedded prompt) wins for the positive prompt.
- The extracted texts are shown in the two **Extracted … prompt** boxes.

## 1b. Layout reference: notes
- A **depth map** is made from the loaded image (Depth Anything V2) and the ControlNet transfers its spatial layout to the new image. Colors, style and details are not taken over.
- **Control image preview** shows the depth map: bright = near, dark = far. Write into the prompt what the depth map cannot see (for example a distant, flat building).
- The image is center-cropped to the **Image size** ratio, so a layout image with a similar ratio is the most accurate.
- **strength**: default **0.9**. Below 0.8 this lite model hardly follows the layout; 1.0 = strict.
- **end_percent**: default **0.6**, so it acts during the first 60% of the steps and the prompt works freely afterwards. If new elements from the prompt (for example a person) do not blend in naturally: 0.4. For a closer copy: 0.8–1.0.
- It affects the base image only. Refine, the detailers and the upscale do not use it.

## 1c. Style reference: notes
- There is no IPAdapter for Z-Image, so the style travels two ways: (1) Florence-2 describes the style image and the Qwen3 text model extracts **only the style** (palette, light, mood, era), and this sentence is added to the **end** of the main prompt; (2) **Color transfer** pulls the colors of the finished base image towards the palette of the style image.
- **The main prompt comes first**: whatever you write (subject, place, weather) overrides the style image. The content of the style image (people, objects) is deliberately not carried over.
- The extracted sentence is shown in the **Extracted style description** box. If you do not like it, edit the lower text of the **Build style-extraction instruction** node (keep `/no_think` at the end, otherwise the answer is empty).
- **Color transfer – strength**: default **0.5**. 0 = no color transfer, 1 = full palette. If your prompt asks for a different palette (for example a cold blue night), use 0–0.2.
- After a new style image the first run takes about half a minute longer (description + extraction); afterwards it is cached.

## 1e. Start image: notes
- The seed still matters: it decides what noise is added to the image. The loaded image replaces the empty canvas.
- **REWRITE AMOUNT (denoise)**: default **0.6**. 0.3–0.5: most of the image stays, only details are redrawn. 0.6–0.8: the image is a loose starting point and the prompt rewrites it strongly. 1.0: the image has no effect.
- **Image size**: the ASPECT RATIO is ignored here. The image keeps its own ratio and is resized to about 1 megapixel (the `megapixels` field of the **Resize** node).
- Applied settings shows whether the start image is active and with what denoise.
- When off, everything works as without it (empty canvas, denoise 1.0). It can be combined with 1b and 1c.

## Trigger and exclusion tags
The THEME selector adds these automatically; you only need to type them with the `None` theme.
- **Trigger tags**: Z-Image Turbo has none, the LoRA does. Put one or two at the **start** of the prompt: `detailed photorealistic cinematic style` (general), `realism style`, `incredibly lifelike` (people), `detailed skin pore` (close-up face), `ultra detailed, sharp` (landscape, building), `Sharp detailed high quality image` (object).
- **Exclusion tags**: the negative prompt box has no effect (CFG 1). Write exclusions at the **end** of the positive prompt: `no text, no watermark, no logos`, for people `correct human anatomy`, for objects `clean plain backdrop, no hands, no people`. Where possible, state what you want instead of what you do not want (`empty street`).
- **Prompt order**: opening tag → framing and subject → environment → light → camera/lens → details → closing exclusions. English, full sentences, 80–250 words.

## Settings per theme
The THEME selector sets these automatically; the exact numbers are in the Preset table, and the ranges below give room for manual fine-tuning. Everywhere: 9 steps, CFG 1, res_multistep.
- **Portrait**: 832×1216 · shift 3 · LoRA 0.8–1.0 · refine 0.25–0.3 · steps: 2, 3 · face denoise 0.2–0.25 · upscale 0.15–0.2. Tags: `close-up portrait`, `85mm lens, f/1.8, shallow depth of field`, `soft window light`, `detailed skin pore`, `sharp focus on the eyes`.
- **People – full body**: 832×1216 or 1216×832 · shift 3–3.5 · LoRA 1.0 · refine 0.3 · steps: 2, 3, 3b (3c if barefoot) · hand 0.35–0.4 · upscale 0.2. Tags: `full-body shot`, `35mm lens`, `candid street photo`, `natural pose`, `unstaged documentary realism`.
- **Landscape – nature**: 1216×832 or 1280×768 · shift 3–4 · LoRA 0–0.4 · refine 0.3–0.4 · steps: 2, 4 · upscale 0.2–0.25. Tags: `ultra-wide landscape shot`, `16mm wide-angle lens, f/11, deep depth of field`, `golden hour`, `soft morning fog`, `sharp foreground detail`.
- **Architecture – cityscape**: 1216×832 or 832×1216 · shift 3.5–4 · LoRA 0.3–0.5 · refine 0.25 · steps: 2, 4, ideally with 1b · upscale 0.15. Tags: `architectural photography`, `straight-on facade view`, `24mm tilt-shift lens, straight vertical lines`, `blue hour with lit windows`, `clean geometric lines`.
- **Interior**: 1216×832 · shift 3–3.5 · LoRA 0.3–0.5 · refine 0.25–0.3 · steps: 2, 4, ideally with 1b · upscale 0.15–0.2. Tags: `interior design photography`, `wide-angle view from the doorway`, `20mm wide-angle lens`, `natural window light`, `linen and wool textures`.
- **Product – object – food**: 1024×1024 · shift 2.5–3 · LoRA 0.3–0.6 · refine 0.25 · steps: 2, 4 · upscale 0.15. Tags: `professional product photo`, `centered composition`, `100mm macro lens, f/8`, `softbox lighting from the left`, `on a seamless white background`.
- **Animal – macro**: 1216×832 or 1024×1024 · shift 2.5–3 · LoRA 0.4–0.7 · refine 0.3–0.35 · steps: 2, 4 (leave 3, 3b, 3c off) · upscale 0.2. Tags: `wildlife photography` / `macro photography`, `400mm telephoto lens, f/4, blurred background`, `individual hairs visible`, `catchlight in the eye`.

## Key settings
- **CFG**: keep it at 1.
- **steps**: 8–10 for the base image.
- **denoise**: refine 0.25–0.4, face 0.10–0.20 (with 4 steps), final upscale 0.15–0.25. A higher value changes more of the image.
- **Rough, grainy skin after the face detailer**: at low denoise with many steps Z-Image Turbo draws grainy skin. That is why the face detailer runs with **4 steps and low denoise**, and **skips large close-up faces** (`force_inpaint` off, `max_size` 1536): on a close-up portrait the refine step has already worked out the face and another pass would only roughen it. Smaller faces (half body, full body) are still processed. To run it on close-up faces too, switch `force_inpaint` back on. For even smoother skin: 3 steps or 0.10 denoise; for more detail: 5 steps. Change the step count first, not the denoise.
- **Image size**: set with the ASPECT RATIO selector: 832×1216 portrait, 1216×832 landscape, 1024×1024 square, 1280×768 wide, 768×1280 tall.

The THEME selector adds these automatically; you only need to type them with the `None` theme.
- **Trigger tags**: Z-Image Turbo has none, the LoRA does. Put one or two at the **start** of the prompt: `detailed photorealistic cinematic style` (general), `realism style`, `incredibly lifelike` (people), `detailed skin pore` (close-up face), `ultra detailed, sharp` (landscape, building), `Sharp detailed high quality image` (object).
- **Exclusion tags**: the negative prompt box has no effect (CFG 1). Write exclusions at the **end** of the positive prompt: `no text, no watermark, no logos`, for people `correct human anatomy`, for objects `clean plain backdrop, no hands, no people`. Where possible, state what you want instead of what you do not want (`empty street`).
- **Prompt order**: opening tag → framing and subject → environment → light → camera/lens → details → closing exclusions. English, full sentences, 80–250 words.

## Settings per theme
The THEME selector sets these automatically; the exact numbers are in the Preset table, and the ranges below give room for manual fine-tuning. Everywhere: 9 steps, CFG 1, res_multistep.
- **Portrait**: 832×1216 · shift 3 · LoRA 0.8–1.0 · refine 0.25–0.3 · steps: 2, 3 · face denoise 0.2–0.25 · upscale 0.15–0.2. Tags: `close-up portrait`, `85mm lens, f/1.8, shallow depth of field`, `soft window light`, `detailed skin pore`, `sharp focus on the eyes`.
- **People – full body**: 832×1216 or 1216×832 · shift 3–3.5 · LoRA 1.0 · refine 0.3 · steps: 2, 3, 3b (3c if barefoot) · hand 0.35–0.4 · upscale 0.2. Tags: `full-body shot`, `35mm lens`, `candid street photo`, `natural pose`, `unstaged documentary realism`.
- **Landscape – nature**: 1216×832 or 1280×768 · shift 3–4 · LoRA 0–0.4 · refine 0.3–0.4 · steps: 2, 4 · upscale 0.2–0.25. Tags: `ultra-wide landscape shot`, `16mm wide-angle lens, f/11, deep depth of field`, `golden hour`, `soft morning fog`, `sharp foreground detail`.
- **Architecture – cityscape**: 1216×832 or 832×1216 · shift 3.5–4 · LoRA 0.3–0.5 · refine 0.25 · steps: 2, 4, ideally with 1b · upscale 0.15. Tags: `architectural photography`, `straight-on facade view`, `24mm tilt-shift lens, straight vertical lines`, `blue hour with lit windows`, `clean geometric lines`.
- **Interior**: 1216×832 · shift 3–3.5 · LoRA 0.3–0.5 · refine 0.25–0.3 · steps: 2, 4, ideally with 1b · upscale 0.15–0.2. Tags: `interior design photography`, `wide-angle view from the doorway`, `20mm wide-angle lens`, `natural window light`, `linen and wool textures`.
- **Product – object – food**: 1024×1024 · shift 2.5–3 · LoRA 0.3–0.6 · refine 0.25 · steps: 2, 4 · upscale 0.15. Tags: `professional product photo`, `centered composition`, `100mm macro lens, f/8`, `softbox lighting from the left`, `on a seamless white background`.
- **Animal – macro**: 1216×832 or 1024×1024 · shift 2.5–3 · LoRA 0.4–0.7 · refine 0.3–0.35 · steps: 2, 4 (leave 3, 3b, 3c off) · upscale 0.2. Tags: `wildlife photography` / `macro photography`, `400mm telephoto lens, f/4, blurred background`, `individual hairs visible`, `catchlight in the eye`.

## Key settings
- **CFG**: keep it at 1.
- **steps**: 8–10 for the base image.
- **denoise**: refine 0.25–0.4, face 0.10–0.20 (with 4 steps), final upscale 0.15–0.25. A higher value changes more of the image.
- **Rough, grainy skin after the face detailer**: at low denoise with many steps Z-Image Turbo draws grainy skin. That is why the face detailer runs with **4 steps and low denoise**, and **skips large close-up faces** (`force_inpaint` off, `max_size` 1536): on a close-up portrait the refine step has already worked out the face and another pass would only roughen it. Smaller faces (half body, full body) are still processed. To run it on close-up faces too, switch `force_inpaint` back on. For even smoother skin: 3 steps or 0.10 denoise; for more detail: 5 steps. Change the step count first, not the denoise.
- **Image size**: set with the ASPECT RATIO selector: 832×1216 portrait, 1216×832 landscape, 1024×1024 square, 1280×768 wide, 768×1280 tall.

    denoise = 1.0
  if denoise < 0.05:
    denoise = 0.05
  i2i = 1
  size_txt = "taken from the start image (about 1 megapixel)"
  start_txt = f"1e ON – rewrite amount (denoise): {denoise}"
refine = preset["refine"]
upscale = preset["upscale"]
groups = preset["groups"]
summary = f"Prompt source: {src_txt}\nTheme: {a}\nImage size: {size_txt}  |  Shift: {shift}  |  LoRA: {lora} ({lora_src})\nStart image: {start_txt}\nRefine denoise: {refine}  |  Upscale denoise: {upscale}\nDefault look: {look_txt}\nRecommended steps: {groups}"
info = f"src={src_code}|theme={a}|w={wid}|h={hei}|i2i={i2i}|denoise={denoise}|shift={shift}|lora={lora}|lora_src={lora_code}|refine={refine}|upscale={upscale}|look={look_code}|steps={groups}"
return (final, wid, hei, shift, lora, refine, upscale, summary, denoise, info)
